title: MapRangeNode — remap float values between ranges
description: Implement a map_range DSL node equivalent to Blender's ShaderNodeMapRange. Remaps a float value from one range to another, with optional clamping. Supports LINEAR and SMOOTH_STEP interpolation modes. This is used extensively in every Blender-Procedural-Human workflow for normalizing distances, creating falloff curves, converting between coordinate spaces, and blending weights. Without this, agents must manually write (value - from_min) / (from_max - from_min) * (to_max - to_min) + to_min inline, which is error-prone and verbose.
definition-of-done:
1. New MapRangeNode class in ixdar-app/src/main/java/ixdar/geometry/mesh/nodes/math/ with @MeshNodeAnnotation id 'map_range'
2. Input ports: value (FloatField), from_min (FloatField, default=0), from_max (FloatField, default=1), to_min (FloatField, default=0), to_max (FloatField, default=1), clamp (BooleanField, default=true), mode (StringField: 'LINEAR' or 'SMOOTH_STEP', default='LINEAR')
3. Output port: result (FloatField)
4. LINEAR mode: standard linear interpolation remap
5. SMOOTH_STEP mode: apply smoothstep (3t^2 - 2t^3) to the normalized value before remapping
6. When clamp=true, clamp output to [to_min, to_max]
7. Works as both scalar and per-vertex field
8. Registered in MeshNodeRegistry and usable in .dsl files
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: map 0.5 from [0,1] to [0,10] — verify result is 5.0
2. Unit test: map 2.0 from [0,1] to [0,10] with clamp=true — verify result is 10.0
3. Unit test: map 2.0 from [0,1] to [0,10] with clamp=false — verify result is 20.0
4. Unit test: SMOOTH_STEP mode — verify smoothed interpolation curve
5. DSL integration: use map_range to remap vertex Y positions, validate with ValidateDsl
